literal: Charity and penance, both of these will not endure in the vast world, if the sky does not give (rain).
translation: If the heavens do not pour down rain, neither charity nor penance will endure in this vast world.
modern: வானம் மழையைத் தராவிட்டால், இந்தப் பரந்த உலகத்தில் தானமும் தவமும் ஆகிய இரண்டும் நிலைபெற்று இருக்காது.
explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute dependence of human moral and spiritual life on rain. The poet states that if the sky fails to give rain, the two fundamental virtues of human society—charity (giving to others) and penance (self-discipline)—will cease to exist in this vast world. Without rain, there is no food or prosperity, making charity impossible; and without basic survival, the mental peace and stability required for spiritual penance are lost. Thus, rain is shown as the essential foundation for both social duty and spiritual practice.
